component.name: Warcraft Rustcorder
component.summary: Automatically record and review World of Warcraft gameplay

description.p: Warcraft Rustcorder captures World of Warcraft activities and keeps a local library for video review with combat-log metadata.
Native Linux and Wayland releases are distributed through the project's signed Flatpak remote. Recordings and configuration remain local.

screenshot.caption: Recording library and player with a combat timeline.

description.p: The app is now called Warcraft Rustcorder. Existing installs move over on their next update with their settings; choose the combat-log and recording folders again in Settings. Warcraft Rustcorder also runs on Windows now, with its own installer and in-app updates.

Each recording now writes only the few seconds of lead-in it needs instead of the whole replay buffer, and finishes with one less video pass. The bundled gpu-screen-recorder is updated to 6.1.3, playing a recording uses less memory, and new installs default to a 60 second replay buffer to hold less RAM while World of Warcraft is open.

Audio settings now list your real output and input devices by name, including virtual microphones. The selected category is remembered across launches, logging out shuts the app down cleanly, and a config file with a bad value is kept as config.json.bad instead of being replaced. The library loads about 3x faster and uses less memory and CPU.
The replay buffer now only runs while World of Warcraft is running, so the GPU's video encoder is idle while the game is closed. Playing a long recording no longer loads the whole file into memory.

The app icon, sidebar logo and tray icon now carry an orange legendary-item border, and the tray always shows the icon of the build that is running. The combat meter's right-click menu shows its Target entry in full instead of hiding it behind a scrollbar.

Much lighter and snappier: the app uses far less memory at idle and in the tray, starts faster, and the download is smaller. The library keeps focus and selection across refreshes, the combat meter animates smoothly, and busy state is shown as toasts. A raid pull or Mythic+ run that started while the previous activity was still ending is now recorded instead of dropped, and several capture, cleanup and memory-leak issues are fixed.

The combat meter gains a Buffs tab showing each player's buff uptime during a pull, and buffs now show their icons instead of being lumped into an "Other" row. Start-up and large libraries are noticeably faster: scanning a big library and actions like tagging or protecting many recordings at once no longer stall the app.

Fixed seek and playback reliability: a seek issued during video preroll no longer wedges all later seeks, and scrubbing back past the first cast of a selected meter spell no longer crashes the app. A second launch of the app no longer moves the running instance's active recording into Recovery. Library, meter, and history rendering is substantially faster on large libraries.

Fixed screen-capture reliability: captures that begin and end in the same moment no longer desynchronize the recorder toggle, and a capture that produces no video file now replaces the recorder so the next recording still saves.

Added a detailed local combat meter alongside each recording, with current-fight and overall views for damage, healing, utility, casts, and deaths; player spell and target breakdowns; and direct seeking into the video. Combat logs carrying the newer UTC-offset timestamp suffix are now parsed correctly.
